text:
anya: quick postmortem draft for the small-req CPU blip after the kernel selector change. findings: tokenization + ingress writev were main hotspots; selector nudged short seqs into multi-kernel path causing per-kernel setup overhead and KV cache fragmentation.

mara: can you summarise action items?

anya: summary + action items:
- immediate: gated selector for seq < 32 (config flag prefer_single_for_short_seq) and bumped ingress coalesce_ms to 8ms for short flows. deployed to 10% canary.
- metrics added: kernel_choice_histogram_by_seq, writev_batch_size_histogram, token_frag_count, kvcache_hit_by_kernel.
- results: combined change lowered host CPU by ~20% on small requests and p99 latency improved ~12ms. KV hit-rate dip observed only when forcing a kernel variant with no local shard warmness; mitigated by warming in the selector path.
- medium-term: refactor kernel_selector cost model to include seq-aware overhead, add microbench for seq range 1..64 in CI, and ensure KV cache keying normalizes across kernel variants to increase cross-variant hits.

ops-lee: adding follow-ups in PERF-17501 and INFRA-3212 for metrics.

shane: also add e2e smoke for tokenization fragmentation and small-write counts in the contract tests so backend changes can't regress writer behavior.

anya: will PR the CI microbench and ticket updates.

perf-bot: [resolve] perf_regression.host_cpu_increase closed on 2026-03-24T15:22:09Z, reason: mitigations rolled and metrics validated.

mara: nice work team. keep the kernel-selector perf tests in CI.
